title: The Woman Who Watches the Moon
summary: An observatory on the peak, a brass telescope pointed at the sky, and a woman who hasn't looked away from it in thirty years.

goals.say: She doesn't look up from the eyepiece. 'You'll want to sit down. Everyone does, the first time.'
goals.name: Hester Quill

threats.name: Hester Quill
threats.target_line: Shh. Don't move. ...There. He blinked. No. No, that was a cloud.
talk: Hester Quill. Astronomer. The valley calls me the Mad Woman of the Peak, which is fair, but incomplete.
The moon. Thirty years of the moon. Do you know it isn't a light in the sky? It's a rock, a world, going round ours. Closer than anyone thinks. You could stand on it.
With fire under you and air in a jar, yes. The overworld isn't all there is. It isn't even most of what there is.
A face. Everyone calls it the man in the moon. Through this glass, on a clear full moon, he has hands. And shoulders. And something across his chest that catches the sun like a blade.
You've noticed it too? The Faithful's eye: a black disc in a ring of gold. That's not an eye. That's an eclipse. The moon in front of the sun. They're praying to something that happened up there.
